notes: Knowledge skill for the tests-first red-green-refactor cycle. Overlaps the test executors, so the boundary case tests that writing tests for already-shipped code routes to unit-test and running a suite routes to run-tests.

evals.prompt: I'm about to build the loyalty-points calculator. Let's do it test-first with TDD.
evals.expected_output: Applies the Three Laws and the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle: writes a failing test first (confirms RED for the right reason), adds the minimum code to pass (GREEN), then refactors while staying green, using the AAA pattern with one behavior per test. Optionally records an ADR.

evals.prompt: Use TDD to add the discount rules engine — write the failing tests before any implementation.
evals.expected_output: Drives the red-green-refactor loop tests-first: prioritizes core business-logic tests, verifies each test fails before writing production code, keeps one logical assertion per test, and refactors after each GREEN.

evals.prompt: Write unit tests for the OrderService we shipped last week.
evals.expected_output: Should route to unit-test, not fire, because the code already exists (tests-after) — tdd-workflow is for tests-first new functionality, NOT for writing tests over done code or running an existing suite (run-tests).
